(3) תחזוקה שוטפת בסיסית;"
law.notes: No provision was found that obliges importers to publish the manufacturer's periodic-maintenance instructions or schedule ("הוראות יצרן לטיפולים תקופתיים" / "תכנית טיפולים") publicly on their website. Searched: the full law text (Hebrew Wikisource transcription, https://he.wikisource.org/wiki/חוק_רישוי_שירותים_ומקצועות_בענף_הרכב), the import/marketing regulations (https://he.wikisource.org/wiki/תקנות_רישוי_שירותים_ומקצועות_בענף_הרכב_(ייבוא_רכב_ושיווקו,_תיווך_בייבוא_אישי_ואגרות)), the garage regulations and the older 1978 import order; nevo.co.il was used to corroborate. The closest provisions: s.80(a)-(b) require providing maintenance and technical information on request to garages, training institutions and others the Minister designates, not to the public or on a website. s.58(b) requires website publication of the importer's service-garage list. Reg.10 requires a usage summary, including "basic routine maintenance", to be delivered to the buyer; it is not a website duty. Champion's books.championmotors.co.il says it publishes this summary under the law. The website-publication duties in the law and regulations cover recalls (reg.8(a)), safety-equipment level (reg.9) and garage-partnership terms and garage lists (s.58). None of these texts addresses automated access, copying, caching or reuse of published material. The quotes come from the Wikisource transcription; the official Reshumot text was not retrieved. Not legal advice.
